transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Alex (ZenSearch Head of Search), Priya (ML Eng), Ben (CTO)

Summary (auto):
Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + reranking flow for ZenSearch's search relevance project. Demo covered embeddings generation, vector store considerations, Redwood's rerank endpoint and candidate scoring, typical latency/cost tradeoffs, and next steps for a short POC using ZenSearch sample data.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain: Elasticsearch + custom BM25 + some in-house embedding experiments
- Demo: embeddings endpoint, similarity search, rerank endpoint with structured scoring, Console routing + monitoring
- Security/compliance: SOC2, data-at-rest KMS, network/VPC options
- Next steps: share pricing, security pack, run rerank POC on sample set

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. I think we have about 45 minutes. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, and Jordan our SE will run the technical demo.
[00:10] Alex: Thanks, Maya. I'm Alex, head of search at ZenSearch. Priya and Ben are with me. We're excited — our search relevance has been underperforming for some queries, especially long-tail.
[00:20] Maya: Yeah totally — and you gave us good context in the form so we'll focus on embeddings + reranking today, show how hosted can slot into your stack quick. Jordan, you want to take it?
[00:30] Jordan: Sure. Quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, how to store vectors, a short demo of our rerank endpoint that takes candidate docs + query and returns a sorted list with scores, and then Console and monitoring.
[00:40] Priya: Quick qualification — do you have hard latency bounds? For some of our premium users we need sub-200ms for rerank, or at least 200–300ms tail.
[00:50] Jordan: Yep that comes up a lot. For hosted we typically see token generation latency in the tens to low hundreds depending on model and batch. For rerank specifically it depends on candidate count. If you're sending 10 candidates, end-to-end is often around 80–250ms using our optimized models — but that's a rough number, we usually benchmark with your corpus.
[01:15] Ben: Are those numbers for your shared hosted tier or dedicated?
[01:20] Jordan: Those are on hosted with our production clusters. Dedicated generally gives more predictable latency and lower tails — it's a capacity reservation. For POC, most customers do hosted to get started, then evaluate Dedicated if they need tighter SLOs.
[01:35] Alex: We're leaning hosted for speed of iteration, but curious about PII and data retention — we can't send raw user PII externally.
[01:45] Maya: Totally — Jordan will drop the security pack after the call. We support customer-managed keys, SOC2, and options to not persist input payloads if you need ephemeral processing.
[01:55] Jordan: And for stricter needs, Redwood Private is used by some regulated customers, but that is a larger lift. For now, hosted with KMS + retention controls is usually enough.
[02:10] Alex: Good. Show us the demo flow from query to rerank?
[02:15] Jordan: Yep, I'll share screen.
[02:30] [screen share noise, slight lag]
[02:35] Jordan: Alright, open the Console — this is the embeddings endpoint. You POST your document or text, we return a 1536-d floating vector (model-dependent). Example: curl example, then our SDK code sample. (note: sample code link: https://redwood.ai/docs/embeddings)
[03:05] Priya: Wait, 1536 — is that for your default model? Can we pick dimension?
[03:10] Jordan: Default for that family is 1536, but we support multiple models with different dims and cost profiles. Usually you pick a model and keep consistent dims for your vector store.
[03:20] Jordan: Next — we recommend storing vectors in a vector DB (Pinecone, Faiss, or Elastic with dense vectors). We also have a built-in similarity API if you want managed storage (note: mentions of Pinecone and Elastic in chat).
[03:40] Alex: We're currently using Elastic with dense vectors. Any gotchas?
[03:45] Jordan: Elastic works but there are perf tradeoffs at scale; Faiss or a managed vector DB often gives better recall/latency. Also consider our prefix/KV cache — if you have repeated prefixes or popular queries, caching reduces cost and latency. (small mis-transcription in notes: "KV cash" appears in auto notes)
[04:05] Priya: How does rerank integrate? Do we send raw documents or ids?
[04:10] Jordan: Two flows: candidate-side rerank where you pass a set of doc IDs and embeddings, or full-text where you pass the actual candidate text. The recommended is to run vector similarity to get top-K candidates and then send those candidate docs plus the query to the rerank endpoint which applies a model that returns a ranked list with confidence scores and a short explanation if you enable structured output.
[04:35] Ben: What's the cost model — per token + per rerank call?
[04:40] Maya: Hosted pricing is usually embeddings per 1k tokens and rerank per call (or per-token depending on model). We'll send an itemized worksheet but typical POC spend for similar customers is low if you keep candidate sizes small and batch embedding ingestion.
[05:00] Alex: Could the rerank endpoint return structured signals for our feature-store? Like reasons (relevance, recency, semantic-match) we can map to our signals?
[05:10] Jordan: Yes — the structured output / function calling can return labeled signals. We can also have the model return token-aligned highlights. That helps explainability and lets you combine model scores with your own heuristics.
[05:30] Priya: Ok show the actual request/response?
[05:35] Jordan: (typing) Here's a sample rerank payload: query, candidates array (each with id, text, embedding), and options {return_explanations: true, model: "redwood-rerank-small"}. Response contains ordered list with score and explanation.
[06:00] [00:06:00] Alex: Is the embedding calculation done synchronously when I call rerank or do we precompute?
[06:05] Jordan: You should precompute embeddings for the corpus and store them. Rerank will often accept embeddings for the candidates to avoid recomputing. For dynamic content you can compute embeddings on-the-fly but that adds latency.
[06:25] Priya: For our dataset of ~10M docs, precompute is obvious, how do you handle versioning when models update?
[06:32] Jordan: We support model versioning and can help with a rollout plan. For large corpora you can do a rolling re-embed with a canary to compare recall differences; our Optimize toolkit can recommend quantization and batching to save costs.
[06:50] Ben: About throughput — if we do a bulk re-embed, can you provide guidance for batching and quant?
[06:56] Jordan: Yes, Optimize will recommend optimal batch sizes and quantization settings by hardware profile. For hosted POC we run the job on our ingestion pipeline or you can run it locally with our tooling.
[07:15] Alex: Any caveats around embeddings drift or recall loss after quantization?
[07:20] Jordan: There's always a tradeoff; small int8 quant can often maintain recall for retrieval but for subtle semantic distinctions you may need higher precision. We'll run evals on your query set and show expected regressions.
[07:40] Priya: Security again — do you persist inputs by default? We need strict retention and audit logs.
[07:48] Jordan: By default we persist minimal logs for debugging, but we can opt out and keep request/response ephemeral. We also have audit logs in the Console and support customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest. We'll share the SOC2 and encryption docs.
[08:05] Maya: Quick pause — any integration blockers on your side for a hosted POC?
[08:10] Alex: Procurement wants to know any vendors in the path — we use SSO, and legal needs to review data flow. Also network wise, we prefer allowing only egress to specific IP ranges or VPC endpoints.
[08:23] Jordan: We provide IP allowlists and have VPC peering options. For stricter controls, Redwood Private. Again, we'll send the network diagram.
[08:34] [demo continues: Jordan runs a live rerank example]
[08:40] Jordan: Here's a sample query "best vegan restaurants near me with outdoor seating". Similarity search returns 50 candidates; rerank takes top 10 and returns ordered results. You can see the explanation tokens — these are short reasons like "semantic match: 0.72; recency: 0.12; popularity: 0.16".
[09:15] Alex: Those scores are nice; can we tune the weighting?
[09:20] Jordan: Yes you can reweight model signals or combine them with your heuristics in the post-process. We support returning the model's raw score and per-feature signals.
[09:34] Priya: Performance question — what about cold starts? If we haven't used a model for hours will first request be slow?
[09:40] Jordan: Cold starts happen but for hosted we mitigate with warm pools for common models. If you need absolute tail guarantees, Dedicated is the right fit.
[09:52] Ben: Is there a way to do A/B between rerank models?
[09:56] Jordan: Yes, the Console supports route-based rollouts and canarying. You can set traffic split and measure CTR/engagement with our eval hooks.
[10:10] Alex: For the POC we want to run a 2-week rerank experiment on a subset of queries and compare metrics — CTR, click pos, and offline relevance. Is that doable?
[10:20] Maya: Absolutely. Typical POC: 2 weeks, run hosted rerank on a sample of queries, Redwood helps with evaluation harness and dashboards. We'll include step-by-step runbooks.
[10:35] Priya: What about rate limits? We have burst traffic — search spikes during marketing campaigns.
[10:40] Jordan: We have quotas and rate-limit tiers; you can request higher throughput or configured burst capacity for Dedicated. For hosted, we can enable burst windows or autoscale behavior.
[10:55] Alex: Can we see Console where you show per-route latency and token-level cost?
[11:00] Jordan: (navigates) Right here — per-route graph, cost per token, top error traces. You can also create alerting for latency or regression on selected prompt sets.
[11:20] Ben: About GDPR/data residency — any region options?
[11:24] Jordan: Yes we have region selection for hosted; EU data residency options available and Private deployment if you need on-prem.
[11:32] Alex: Ok, procurement is likely to ask about indemnity — I know that's legal, but any standard limits?
[11:38] Maya: We'll route legal to legal; typical enterprise SLA and contract. We'll also provide our compliance package.
[11:45] [pause — quick clarifying Q/A]
[12:00] Priya: One technical nit — if we pass embeddings in the rerank call, what format do you accept? Float32 arrays? base64?
[12:06] Jordan: Float arrays in JSON are fine; we also accept base64 for binary. SDKs handle serialization.
[12:20] Alex: For POC dataset, we'll likely provide S3 with a temp prefix. Any minimum format?
[12:25] Jordan: A CSV/JSONL with id, text, metadata fields is ideal. We'll share an example.
[12:34] Maya: Great — let's talk timeline. What does ZenSearch want?
[12:38] Alex: We'd like to run POC next two weeks and have results for internal review by end of month. Procurement might take 2–3 weeks but we can start the technical work.
[12:48] Ben: If we start technical work before procurement sign, what are the risks?
[12:52] Maya: We often do a low-touch POC under an MSA or with limited scoped engagement. Jordan will outline minimal data and risk controls.
[13:05] Priya: For evaluation metrics, can you run automatic diffed evals between baseline BM25+our current rerank vs Redwood rerank?
[13:12] Jordan: Yes, our evals harness can compute recall@k, MRR, nDCG and export comparison charts.
[13:25] Alex: Any prominent known regressions your customers see?
[13:29] Jordan: Usually small precision/recall tradeoffs when moving to aggressive quant; semantic rerank helps most long-tail queries. We'll show the expected delta on your sample set.
[13:45] [screen share: Console - routes and monitoring]
[14:00] Maya: We'll recap next steps at the end. For now Jordan, any final things to demo?
[14:05] Jordan: I'll show the rerank request/response live once more and the eval page. (runs a couple requests)
[14:30] [live run: shows request latency ~140ms for 10 candidates]
[14:40] Priya: That's promising. Can we run a bigger candidate set? Say 50?
[14:45] Jordan: Yes but latency grows linearly; 50 candidates we saw ~300–450ms on hosted for this model — again depends on model and batching. That's where candidate trimming + hybrid approach helps.
[15:05] Alex: Hybrid meaning combining sparse signals with vector?
[15:10] Jordan: Right — use BM25 to get a smaller candidate set, then do vector similarity and rerank. That gives good recall with lower cost.
[15:25] Ben: How do we measure cost impact?
[15:28] Jordan: Console's cost breakdown shows token/embedding costs per route and you can filter by date and tag. We'll give you an example cost model for your projected QPS.
[15:40] Alex: For the POC we'll try hosted and see if performance is fine; if not we'll look at Dedicated.
[15:48] Maya: Sounds good. Jordan, any security docs to call out?
[15:52] Jordan: SOC2 Type II, ISO certs, KMS options, SAML SSO, role-based access controls. We'll attach the pack.
[16:05] [closing — recap & next steps]
[16:10] Maya: Ok quick recap: Maya to send pricing worksheet and POC template; Jordan to send security pack and network diagram; ZenSearch (Alex/Priya) to share sample queries and S3 dataset. We'll schedule a joint benchmark week of 9/27. Anything to add?
[16:30] Alex: No, that covers it. We'll try to get the dataset to you by 9/20.
[16:35] Ben: I'll review procurement timeline and circle back.
[16:40] Priya: I'll prep the query set and baseline eval scripts.
[16:45] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links.
[16:50] [end meeting]
